evidence: Description of experimental methods used in the study, illustrated in Figure 1

claim: A431 cells are an EGFR-overexpressing squamous-cell carcinoma cell line
source: Cells were starved overnight, stimulated with 25 ng/ml EGF, flash frozen at multiple time points post-stimulation, and lysates run on LDS-PAGE in duplicate. All blots included positive and negative pY controls to assess non-specific binding. Blots were probed with recombinant GST-tagged SH2 and PTB probes and an anti-pY antibody (Supplementary file 1) (Machida et al., 2007). Of the probes tested, 27 were selected for further analysis based on significant, reproducible, and dynamic binding to EGF-stimulated A431 cell lysates (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1). Anti-pY blots of the same lysates showed a rapid increase in total phosphorylation upon EGF treatment, dominated by a major band corresponding to EGFR (Figure 2A, top panel).
evidence: Supported by citations to Stanton et al., 1994 and Wrann and Fox, 1979

claim: 27 SH2/PTB probes were selected for further analysis based on significant, reproducible, and dynamic binding to EGF-stimulated A431 cell lysates
source: Of the probes tested, 27 were selected for further analysis based on significant, reproducible, and dynamic binding to EGF-stimulated A431 cell lysates (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Based on experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: Anti-pY blots showed a rapid increase in total phosphorylation upon EGF treatment, dominated by a major band corresponding to EGFR

evidence: Based on experimental data shown in Figure 2A

claim: Five highly dynamic bands were identified with three well-defined kinetic patterns: EGFR, p130CAS (doublet), GAB1, and SHCA
source: Most prominent were five highly dynamic bands, which were identified by immunodepletion (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–D) and exhibited three well-defined kinetic patterns. These major bands were (1) EGFR, a ~195 kDa band whose phosphorylation increased rapidly following EGF treatment, dipped slightly and then remained relatively constant; (2 and 3) the focal adhesion protein p130CAS, a doublet at 150 and 115 kDa whose phosphorylation was high in unstimulated cells, decreased rapidly upon EGF treatment, and then rebounded at later time points; (4) the scaffolding protein GAB1, a single band at 130 kDa that was phosphorylated with kinetics similar to EGFR, then rapidly returned to near basal levels; and (5) the scaffold/adaptor SHCA, a relatively weak band at 71 kDa which displayed kinetics similar to that of EGFR (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Based on experimental data from immunodepletion and far-Western blotting
